newsitem.title: UK: Laird jumps on Merrill upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Laird jumps on Merrill upgrade.

text.p: Shares in Laird Group Plc jumped to its highest level in more than four months after Merrill Lynch issued a 40-page "buy" note on the stock.
AT 1121 GMT, the shares were up 14p to 412-1/2 amid a generally flat to weaker UK engineering sector.
Merrill analyst Adam Collins said he had raised his recommendation to "buy" from "neutral," and said he expected the share price to rise to 566p to 590p within a year.
"This is a growth story and the stock is too cheap," said Collins, who was estimating double-digit earnings growth in 1998 and 1999.
He was forecasting 1997 pre-tax profits of 69.1 million stg and 1998 and 1999 profits of 79 million stg and 90 million stg, respectively.

Growth, he said, would be boosted by the company's auto parts unit as it secured new contracts in the U.S. and grabbed a greater portion of the European market. Those operations alone would enjoy organic growth of some 30 percent, Collins said.
His estimates took into account the strength of sterling. He said he had factored in an exchange rate of 2.70 German marks.
The pound was trading around 2.787 marks on Thursday morning.
